title: getStaticProps in Depth
description: Master dynamic parameters, revalidation, notFound, and redirects for static pages.

slides.title: Dynamic Routes & getStaticPaths 🛤️
slides.content:
# Static Generation for Dynamic Pages

If a page has dynamic segments like `[id].js`, you need to tell Next.js **which paths** to pre‑render.

Export `getStaticPaths` to return a list of possible values.

Then `getStaticProps` receives the params to fetch data for that specific instance.

```
pages/posts/[id].js
```

slides.title: Dynamic Static Page (pages/posts/[id].js)
slides.content: Pre‑render a specific set of posts at build time.

quizData.question: What is the purpose of `getStaticPaths`?

options.text: To define which dynamic routes should be pre‑rendered at build time
To fetch data for the current page

quizData.explanation: For dynamic routes, `getStaticPaths` tells Next.js which instances to generate during the build.

slides.title: fallback: false, true, or 'blocking' 🔀
slides.content:
# Handling Paths Not Returned by getStaticPaths

* **`fallback: false`** – any path not listed returns 404.
* **`fallback: true`** – Next.js will generate the page on the first request (client‑side).
* **`fallback: 'blocking'`** – server‑side generate on first request, then cache (no loading state).

Choose based on how many pages you have and how often new content appears.

slides.title: fallback: true with Loading State (pages/posts/[id].js)
slides.content: When `fallback: true`, the page component must handle the loading state with `router.isFallback`.

quizData.question: When would you use `fallback: 'blocking'`?

options.text: When you want a custom loading spinner
When you want to return a 404 immediately
When you don't want to show a loading state and prefer to wait for the page to be generated on the server
When the page is static and never changes

quizData.explanation: `'blocking'` tells Next.js to SSR the first request completely before sending the response. No loading state needed.

slides.title: Pro Tip 💡
slides.content: Combine `revalidate` with `fallback: 'blocking'` for large e‑commerce sites: you can pre‑build top products and generate the rest on demand, then cache them.
